title: Tests Returning Result
goal: Return a Result from test functions to use the question mark operator cleanly.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Unit Tests

sections.text: By default, test functions return `()` and fail by panicking. You can also define a test function that returns `Result<(), E>`.

sections.caption: Returning Result allows using ? inside test functions.

sections.text: When a test returns `Err(...)`, Cargo counts it as a test failure. You do not need to call `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` everywhere.
The error type `E` must implement the `std::fmt::Debug` trait so Cargo can print the failure details.

sections.caption: The test passes on Ok(()) and fails when returning an Err value.

sections.text: You cannot combine `#[should_panic]` with a test function that returns `Result`. The compiler rejects this combination.

explanation: Return a Result from test functions to use the question mark operator cleanly.
